spec.title: PROP-076 — The cache-stable SYSTEM prompt prefix
spec.p: Framework record, owner request 2026-11-07; design settled 2026-11-10 against the tree at `e2508fc1d`. Status `spec/plan`: nothing is implemented. The owner's shape is the research proposal `campaigns/next-semantic-transfer-2026-11/architecture/SYSTEM-PROMPT-SPEC.md` and its machine form `system-prompt.json`; the decisions below settle every choice that document left open, against the actual code rather than against the 2026-11-07 survey, which carried seven wrong file paths and three wrong behavioural claims (`#SYS-BASELINE-CORRECTIONS`). Implementation follows the corporate-environment and application-version campaigns (campaign node `SYS-PROMPT`, after `APP-VERSIONS`); the plan is `campaigns/sys-prompt-2026-11/PLAN.md`. This document is a design, not an acceptance: no fact below is evidence that any part of the feature exists.

p.SYS-PURPOSE: A project can hand an API caller one byte-stable block of instructions instead of asking an agent to re-read its boot lane. The user writes `vibevm/vibespecs/boot/SYSTEM-TEMPLATE.md` — ordinary permanent instructions, no language, no directives — and `vibe` generates `vibevm/vibespecs/boot/SYSTEM.md`: the user's frame, the selected repository entrypoint, and the already-compiled static boot lane, in one deterministic UTF-8 text fit for the instruction role of an API request. The same relevant inputs always give the same bytes, so a provider that caches on an exact prefix match can cache it; a change of task never changes it; and a stale copy is detected before a request is sent rather than silently believed. The live part of boot — the current INDEX inputs and the session's own context — follows that prefix at request time and is never frozen into it. What this buys is the *conditions* for a cache hit and an honest freshness claim, never a promised hit, TTL or percentage saved.

p.SYS-SIZE-TODAY: The scale, measured on this repository at `e2508fc1d`, is why the feature exists: the compiled lane `vibevm/vibespecs/boot/STATIC.xml` is 251,817 bytes, the entrypoint `AGENTS.md` is 26,121 bytes, and the eight files `vibevm/vibespecs/boot/INDEX.md` names are 57,894 bytes together — 335,832 bytes of boot material, of which **75% is the one compiled lane** and **92% (the lane plus the entrypoint) changes only when packages, authored boot sources or the template change**. That 92% is the prefix this document specifies. The remaining 8% is the continuation, which is byte-stable too but stays late-bound on purpose (`#SYS-NO-FROZEN-INDEX`).

boundary.title: 2. The prefix and the live continuation

p.SYS-BANDS: **Decided 2026-11-10 — four bands, and exactly one of them is a generated file.** **Band P, the prefix**: the bytes of `SYSTEM.md`, in three segments — the literal template, the entrypoint export, and the compiled static lane. **Band U, the unconditional continuation**: the admitted bytes of every INDEX entry with no residual `when`, in INDEX order. **Band G, the gated continuation**: every INDEX entry carrying a residual `when`, each evaluated against an explicitly supplied session target. **Band T, the task**: the session context, the conversation and the request. Band P is a committed artifact; bands U and G are a *plan* in `SYSTEM.meta.json` that a runner executes at request time by reading the current files; band T is the caller's own and never appears in any witness. The pair (P, U+G) covers the whole **computable** boot of the selected node; band T is everything else. The four-band split is the whole design: it is what lets the big stable text be a file while the late-bound text stays late-bound.

p.SYS-BAND-ORDER: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the order inside band P, and why the boot law and the cache agree.** The three segments are, in order: **(1)** the template, **(2)** the entrypoint export, **(3)** the static lane. That is PROP-009 `#SESSION-START-ORDER` with the user's own frame prepended — redirect, then `STATIC`, then (in bands U and G) the INDEX entries — so no authored instruction is reordered relative to any other. It is *also* the cache-optimal order, which is the design's one piece of luck and is recorded so nobody "optimises" it later: a provider cache matches a **prefix**, so an edit to an early segment invalidates every later one. The lane is the segment that changes most often (every `vibe install` that moves the resolution can move it) and the template is the segment that changes least often (a human edits it deliberately, rarely), so putting the lane **last** means a lane change costs only the lane's own cache entry, while the reverse order would make every lane change invalidate the template and the entrypoint too. The two constraints point the same way; neither is being traded against the other.

p.SYS-NOT-COMPLETE-BOOT: **`SYSTEM.md` alone is not a session.** The prefix is not declared a snapshot of everything a session needs, and a caller that sends it alone gets an explicitly incomplete boot. Obligations an authored entrypoint states beyond reading files — resolve a user-local context, read a plan, consult a campaign document — are not discharged by generation and are not reported as discharged: an agent with tools performs them, or the calling program supplies the material through its own runtime contract. An exporter never claims to have read what it did not read. This is the honest boundary, stated once, so that no later convenience ("ship the one file") can be mistaken for a complete contract.

p.SYS-NO-FROZEN-INDEX: **Decided 2026-11-10 — `kind = "static"` in INDEX is not permission to compile.** An INDEX row's `kind` describes *read timing*, not linkage: PROP-009 `#AUTHORED-INDEX-BOUNDARY` says so in words and `crates/vibe-workspace/src/boot_artifacts.rs:203-207` says so in code, where the kind is literally `if e.when.is_some() { "dynamic" } else { "static" }` over entries that `crates/vibe-workspace/src/boot.rs:314`/`:336` have already forced to `LinkType::Dynamic` + `PackageFormat::Simple`. PROP-072 `#SOURCE-HOST-BOOT-LAW` repeats the rule from the source side. Therefore no INDEX entry's bytes enter `SYSTEM.md`, however unconditional the row, and a second "freeze the whole INDEX" profile is **not** offered in this version: it would contradict dynamic linking, make freshness far harder to prove, and buy nothing that `#SYS-CONTINUATION-CACHEABLE` does not already buy. A target-bound full snapshot remains a separate contract for a separate request, named in `#SYS-OWNER-QUESTIONS` Q1.

p.SYS-CONTINUATION-CACHEABLE: **Decided 2026-11-10 — band U is cacheable without being frozen, and that is the whole reason the boundary costs nothing.** Band U's bytes are the current bytes of files whose *identity and order* the boot plan fixes; they change only when those files change, exactly as band P's do. A provider that supports several cache breakpoints can therefore place one at the end of band P and another at the end of band U, and a task change still invalidates neither. `prepare` makes this possible by returning bands P, U, G and the recommended breakpoint positions **as separate, ordered materials with their own observed digests**, not as one concatenated string. So the design gives up nothing by keeping INDEX late-bound: the bytes are cached either way, and the one thing not given up is the runtime meaning of a dynamic entry. The only residual cost against a frozen artifact is that a runner must read band U's files per request, which is local file reading of 57,894 bytes on this repository.

p.SYS-FILES: **Decided 2026-11-10 — three paths, three roles, under the selected node's `vibevm/vibespecs/boot/`.** `SYSTEM-TEMPLATE.md` is **authored** by the user: literal permanent text, the only input the user writes, never rewritten by `vibe`. `SYSTEM.md` is **generated**: the prefix bytes of `#SYS-BANDS`, git-tracked and marked generated like `STATIC`/`INDEX` (PROP-009 `#ARTIFACTS-GENERATED`), so a fresh clone boots by pure file reading and never by running a build. `SYSTEM.meta.json` is **generated**: the versioned sidecar of `#SYS-SIDECAR` — the input witnesses, the segment map and the continuation plan. Editing `SYSTEM.md` by hand is not a supported way to configure anything; the supported way is the template and `#SYS-MANIFEST-TABLE`. The `.md` extension of `SYSTEM.md` is a name, not a parse: nothing reads the file as Markdown, and its lane segment holds XML bytes verbatim (`#SYS-LANE-VERBATIM`).

p.SYS-OPT-IN: **Decided 2026-11-10 — presence of the template is the opt-in, and nothing else is.** No template, no generation and no change whatever to the node's boot: `vibe install` behaves byte-for-byte as it does today, which is what makes this feature free for every project that does not want it. A present but empty template means "opt in with no frame of my own" and generates a prefix of the entrypoint export plus the lane. `vibe init` may **offer** to create a template; no installation ever creates, overwrites or deletes an authored template. Opting out is deleting the template, which removes only the two provably-owned generated outputs (`#SYS-REMOVAL-AND-CONFLICT`).

p.SYS-TEMPLATE-LITERAL: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the template is text, not a program, and this version introduces no template language at all.** There is no shell, no environment or `HOME` read, no `INCLUDE`, no network, no conditionals, no slot grammar and no placement directives. Curly braces, fenced examples, Markdown links and the literal strings `SYSTEM.md` or `<vibevm>` inside the template are ordinary characters with no effect — which is the point of `#SYS-SELF-INCLUSION`'s rule that self-reference is judged over semantic edges, never over prose. `vibe` appends the two contract-defined segments after the template's bytes; where they go is fixed by `#SYS-BAND-ORDER` and is not the author's choice. Controlled placement (a declared insertion point) is a later, separate extension, and deliberately not this version's problem: the useful feature does not need it, and a grammar is the one thing that cannot be taken back.

p.SYS-MANIFEST-TABLE: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the tuning that is not text goes in the manifest, following PROP-075 `#TEMPLATE-SPELLING` exactly.** One new optional top-level table `[system_prompt]` on the node's own `vibe.toml`, with exactly three optional members in this version: `entrypoint` (a relative path, default `"AGENTS.md"`, admitted only from the closed set `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `GEMINI.md` — the same set `crates/vibe-workspace/src/boot_artifacts/redirect.rs:29` already owns — or the boolean `false` meaning "no entrypoint segment"), `lane_form` (`"verbatim"`, the default and in this version the only accepted value, reserved so `#SYS-LANE-VERBATIM`'s alternative needs no format change), and `recipe` (an integer pinning the generated-text recipe of `#SYS-TRANSPORT-CONTRACT`; absent means the current one). `[system_prompt]` present with no `SYSTEM-TEMPLATE.md` beside it is a validation refusal naming the TOML path, by the rule of PROP-059 `#declaration` that every refusal names its field as a TOML path; the table must be added to `Manifest`, to `ManifestWire` (`deny_unknown_fields`) and to both `TryFrom` arms or it is refused as unknown. Every member is omitted when absent, so every existing manifest serialises byte-identically. Nothing else is configurable in this version — no inclusion policy, no segment order, no OS baking.

p.SYS-LAYOUT-RESERVATION: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the three paths join the one shared layout owner, each in its own role, and the research's "do not label the template generated" warning is honoured literally.** `crates/vibe-core/src/layout.rs` gains `SYSTEM_MD`, `SYSTEM_META_JSON` and `SYSTEM_TEMPLATE_MD` beside `INDEX_MD` (`:72`), `STATIC_XML` (`:74`) and `STATIC_MD` (`:76`), with `current_boot_system()`, `current_boot_system_meta()` and `current_boot_system_template()` beside `current_boot_index()` (`:216`). The private `generated_boot_paths()` (`:250`) gains the two **generated** paths, so `is_generated_boot_output` (`:241`) and `is_reserved_boot_source` (`:268`) cover them with their existing exact-match and ASCII-case-alias semantics and all twelve existing callers inherit the exclusion at once. The **authored** template gets a *separate* predicate `is_reserved_boot_authored_input`, not membership in `generated_boot_paths`: it is excluded from automatic boot enrolment and from declaration admission as a source row, but it is not generated, is not owned by publication, is never deleted as a stale output, and is preserved like any authored file. Collapsing the two roles into one list would be the convenient mistake that loses the template on a format change.

p.SYS-SELF-INCLUSION: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the exact hazard, the exact three gates, and the exact test for self-reference.** The hazard is real today and not hypothetical: `crates/vibe-workspace/src/install/bootgen/own_boot.rs:167` `legacy_entries` enumerates the immediate children of the boot directory and admits every one that `vibe_specdoc::is_spec_source` accepts — which is, by extension alone, every `.md` and `.xml` file (`crates/vibe-specdoc/src/load.rs:76-81`) — excluding only `STATIC.md`, `STATIC.xml` and `INDEX.md` by name (`:185-190`). Dropped in unprepared, `SYSTEM.md` and `SYSTEM-TEMPLATE.md` would both become ordinary boot inputs: the generated prefix would be compiled into its own successor on the next install (recursive growth), and the template's text would be delivered twice. The three gates that must all learn the names are therefore **(a)** the legacy immediate-children scan above, **(b)** the automatic native discovery in `crates/vibe-spec/src/source_policy/authored_boot.rs:74-129`, which already skips generated outputs at `:97` through `is_generated_boot_output` and so inherits the two generated paths for free, needing an explicit arm only for the authored template, and **(c)** declaration admission, `crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/source_descriptor/mod.rs:228`, which already refuses generated boot outputs including ASCII case aliases. **The test for self-reference is an admitted semantic edge or a file identity, never a string.** A template that discusses `SYSTEM.md`, links to it in Markdown, or shows it in a fenced example is ordinary literal text and is admitted; a declared source row, a boot snippet binding or a path alias that actually resolves to one of the three paths is refused **before** anything is written, naming the path and the edge. An output listed in its own inputs, directly or through any alias the layout owner recognises, is the same refusal.

p.SYS-ENTRYPOINT-ONE: **Decided 2026-11-10 — exactly one entrypoint, of the selected node, never a filesystem walk.** The default is the selected node's own `AGENTS.md`; `#SYS-MANIFEST-TABLE` may name `CLAUDE.md` or `GEMINI.md` instead, or `false` for none. The three are never concatenated: by this repository's own convention they are kept byte-identical, so joining them triples the text, and in a project where they differ by harness, joining them delivers contradictions. Ancestor or external instruction files are not discovered by walking the filesystem: inheritance is whatever the selected-node effective-boot contract already computes (PROP-009 `#FOUNDATION-DOWN`, `#MATRYOSHKA-SCOPES`), and an explicitly added harness input appears in the sidecar's input list like any other. A node with no entrypoint file and no `false` declaration is a refusal naming the expected path, not a silent empty segment.

p.SYS-REDIRECT-IN-PLACE: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the managed block is replaced in place, at its own byte range, and nothing else in the document is touched.** The entrypoint carries a vibe-owned `<vibevm>` managed block (PROP-009 `#REDIRECT-MANAGED-BLOCK`, PROP-012) whose whole content is boot instructions. `crates/vibe-workspace/src/boot_artifacts/redirect.rs:128` `locate_block` already returns that block's exact `start`/`end` byte offsets, refuses a malformed or mismatched marker pair rather than repairing it, and matches only an exactly standalone `<vibevm>` / `</vibevm>` line. The export takes the entrypoint's admitted bytes, and substitutes the transport contract of `#SYS-TRANSPORT-CONTRACT` for exactly the bytes between those offsets. Three consequences, each deliberate: the generated text sits in the one position where generated text already sits today, so no authored paragraph moves; the authored preamble that also orders a full boot is answered at the same relative distance it is answered today; and a malformed marker pair is a named refusal, never a regex repair of a co-tenant document. A node whose entrypoint has no managed block at all is admitted with its bytes whole and the contract appended as its own trailing segment — stated here so the common case and the no-block case do not need two readings of the same rule.

p.SYS-NO-REWRITE-OF-AUTHORED-TEXT: **The exporter never summarises, shortens, reorders or filters authored instructions.** No model touches the text; no heuristic decides a paragraph is "not suitable for an API"; no absolute path an author wrote is edited away. The one structurally-owned region named in `#SYS-REDIRECT-IN-PLACE` is the only substitution. The generator's own restriction against volatile content (`#SYS-NO-VOLATILE`) binds the generator, not the author: an authored absolute path, machine fact or operating-facts ledger entry passes through verbatim, and the most diagnostics may do is *report* that such content makes the prefix less portable or more volatile. It never changes policy silently, and a warning is not a licence to edit.

p.SYS-TRANSPORT-CONTRACT: **Decided 2026-11-10 — what the one piece of generated prose says, and what it carefully does not say.** The contract is a short, versioned, generated block (`recipe`, `#SYS-MANIFEST-TABLE`) that states, as plain facts about this request: which sources have been supplied in it, each by role and relative path; that their content is already present and need not be read again **to discharge those same boot obligations**; that the continuation entries actually supplied are named where they appear; and that any entry not named has **not** been supplied and must not be treated as read. It is the honest answer to the problem that some authored paragraphs legitimately order a `STATIC` read: rather than guessing which sentences those are and editing them, the transport states what transport did. Four things it must not do. It does not forbid tool calls in general — a later instruction to check the current state of a file on disk remains perfectly valid, and no text can guarantee an agent makes no tool call anyway; that is a property of the adapter and of agent behaviour, proved by `#SYS-ROLE-PLACEMENT`'s tests, not asserted by prose. It does not instruct the agent to run `vibe` or anything else: PROP-009 `#PURE-FILE-READING` and `#REJ-RUN-VIBE` forbid turning boot into a command, and `prepare` is the *calling program's* preflight, never the model's errand (`#SYS-READ-ONLY-CHECK`). It carries no digest, build time, path or counter, so it cannot be the thing that makes two otherwise equal prefixes differ. And it speaks only for its own layer, which is what lets `#SYS-LAYER-CONCATENATION` add more layers later without rewriting it.

p.SYS-ENTRYPOINT-IS-AN-INPUT: **The entrypoint is a build input, so a prefix can change with no package change at all.** Editing the entrypoint's authored prose — a new convention, a corrected rule, a line in an operating-facts ledger — changes the prefix, and the generator does not hide that to protect a cache. The claim this design makes is "the same relevant inputs give the same bytes", never "unchanged until the package list changes". The honest consequence is that a repository whose entrypoint carries frequently-edited current-state material pays a cache write per edit; the remedy is to move that material out of the entrypoint, which is a repository-hygiene decision for its owner and not something the exporter may take on their behalf.

p.SYS-LANE-VERBATIM: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the lane enters as the admitted bytes, opaque, and is not re-parsed, re-compiled or projected.** `vibe` has a read-only in-memory analyser that shares composer, table, hoist, de-substitution, source bindings and freshness admission with the write path (`crates/vibe-workspace/src/install/bootgen/analyze.rs`, whose provider-free `analyze_node_lane` at `:80` ends in an in-memory compile at `:216`), and **three** independent lane prepare-and-compile sites, each with its own `entries.is_empty() → None` gate — the builtin seam `boot_artifacts/compile.rs:86` `compile_static_artifact_with_plans` (`:100-103`), the owner-managed seam `boot_artifacts/native_managed.rs:232` (`:260-263`), and the custom-backend seam `boot_artifacts/native_managed/explicit.rs:22` (`:35-38`). The prefix reuses that output as **one admitted segment**, through whichever of the three the node's own world selects — it does not add a fourth, and it does not assume one; it never re-enters the compiler as a fresh normal source, which would risk doubled qualification, lost attribution and duplicate expansion, and it never follows a `#use` marker, a provenance comment or a `spec://` reference found in the text. Three mechanisms in the lane keep their meaning untouched because nothing reads inside the segment: normal-closure source-identity coverage (PROP-009 `#NORMAL-CLOSURE-ONCE`), compiled-unit de-substitution with its deliberate partial-coverage residual (`#STATIC-EMITS-ONCE-EACH`), and soft hoisting's `#use` markers. The alternative — an explicitly selected canonical Markdown projection through PROP-072 `#SOURCE-GENERATED-XML-PROJECTION-LAW` — is **rejected for this version** and reserved as `lane_form = "projected"`: it would make a prompt build fail on an unrepresentable placement, and it changes the token stream, which would confound the one differential proof this campaign has (that the prefix delivers what a file-reading agent reads). Original generated bytes and any future projected bytes are different facts with different digests, and the sidecar would name which it holds.

p.SYS-LANE-SPELLING: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the lane's spelling and absence are the existing owner's answers, not the exporter's.** Which of `STATIC.md` / `STATIC.xml` exists is decided by `crates/vibe-workspace/src/boot_artifacts/format.rs:42` `resolve_static_path`, which returns the one present path, `None` when neither is present, and a **refusal** when both are (`:50-55`, "the generator owns one; delete the stray"). The exporter retains all three answers exactly: it records the selected spelling in the sidecar, it builds a valid prefix with **no** lane segment when a node has no static contributions, and it propagates the both-present refusal rather than picking a side. A first generation on a node that has never had a lane is therefore a normal case, not an error, and the analyser's dialect fallback for an uncommitted spelling is reported rather than silently resolved.

p.SYS-SEGMENT-FRAMING: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the exact framing, because determinism lives in these details.** Each segment is introduced by a single frame line of a fixed generated form carrying the layer-qualified segment id and nothing variable — no digest, no length, no time, no path of the checkout. The frame token is distinct from the lane's own `vibe:c1` comments and is never an exactly standalone `<vibevm>` or `</vibevm>` line, so `locate_block` can never mistake a frame for a managed marker and a frame can never be mistaken for lane content. **Frames use LF and the file ends with exactly one LF**; a segment **body** is the admitted bytes verbatim, with one LF inserted before the next frame when the body does not already end with one, so an authored CRLF document keeps its own line endings inside its own segment and the surrounding structure is identical on every host. The repository-wide `* text=auto eol=lf` of `.gitattributes:7` is what makes that identity survive a Windows checkout, and the determinism claim of `#SYS-DETERMINISM` depends on it — a project without that attribute gets a prefix that differs by checkout, which diagnostics report. Text separators are structure for a reader, never a security boundary: `#SYS-ROLE-PLACEMENT` says the same thing about roles.

identity.title: 6. Identity, freshness and determinism

p.SYS-TWO-IDENTITIES: **Two different facts, never conflated.** `prefix_sha256` is the digest of the bytes actually in `SYSTEM.md` — it proves byte identity and nothing else. The **input witness** is the ordered list of the observed inputs the text was built from, together with the selected node, entrypoint, recipe, lane spelling and boot-plan identity — it proves *consistency* between an output and a set of observations. Neither proves authenticity: the existing boot-graph verifier is graph verification and explicitly not body authentication (PROP-072 `#SOURCE-BOOT-CHECK-LAW`), and the existing unit fingerprint (`crates/vibe-workspace/src/boot/hybrid/fingerprint.rs:133` `compute`) hashes identity, own path, resolved version, conditions, fragments, edge modes, child fingerprints, optional owner-plan digests and native-pending frames and performs **no file read at all** — so it cannot stand in for an input witness, and the node lane carries no fingerprint anyway (`boot_artifacts.rs:379`, `:394-395`). A matching digest with a matching witness means "this text is what these observations produce"; it never means "these observations are trustworthy" or "this prefix is what a provider cached".

p.SYS-SIDECAR: **Decided 2026-11-10 — what version 1 of the sidecar holds, and the four things it must not hold.** `SYSTEM.meta.json`, protocol `vibe-system-prompt/1`, described by a new JTD schema and a new format-registry record (`#SYS-FORMAT-CHANGES`): the protocol tag; the **relative** identity of the selected node; the entrypoint's relative path or `false`; the recipe version; the lane spelling (`static-md` / `static-xml` / `none`) and `lane_form`; the `layer` role (`#SYS-LAYER-ROLE`); an ordered `inputs[]` of the prefix's inputs, each with its role, its path relative to the node, the SHA-256 of the bytes **as observed** and their length; `prefix_sha256` and `prefix_len`; a `segments[]` map of id, byte offset, length and whether the segment is recommended as a cache boundary; the boot-plan identity the existing owner produces, together with the SHA-256 of `INDEX.md`'s bytes; and the `continuation` plan — the ordered rows of bands U and G, each with its path relative to the node, its band, and for a gated row its `when` string verbatim. **It must not hold**: a build time or any timestamp; an absolute checkout, `HOME` or cache path; the generating host's operating system or any environment observation; and **no content digest for any continuation row** — the reason is `#SYS-CONTINUATION-WITNESS-IS-RUNTIME`. A sidecar is therefore a pure function of the prefix inputs and the boot plan, which is what makes a second `vibe install` with nothing changed produce byte-identical files and no git diff.

p.SYS-CONTINUATION-WITNESS-IS-RUNTIME: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the continuation's bytes are witnessed per request, never in the committed artifact, and this is the decision that keeps dynamic linking meaningful.** Putting a hash of `90-user.xml` in the sidecar would make every edit of a user boot snippet dirty a committed generated file and demand a regeneration — destroying the one property dynamic linking exists for, that an authored snippet's bytes may change and be read fresh without a rebuild. So the committed witness covers the prefix inputs and the *plan* (its order, its paths, its conditions, the digest of the `INDEX.md` bytes that fix them), and `prepare` reports the continuation's observed digests in its **response**, as request-local observations. The practical rule follows directly and is the one in `#SYS-INVALIDATION`: changed dynamic bytes under an unchanged plan give a new suffix and leave the prefix valid; a changed plan — a new, removed or reordered entry, a changed condition, changed visibility, a different selected node or a different package binding — invalidates the pairing and must be recomputed under the current world rather than paired blindly with an old prefix.

p.SYS-NO-VOLATILE: **The generator inserts nothing volatile into the stable bytes.** No build time, no absolute checkout or `HOME` path, no Git branch, HEAD or dirty state, no task or plan state, no session or run id, no model name, no token or size estimate, and no result of environment detection. No whole-build digest is placed **before** the large repeatable content either: a digest at the top would make every change to a late segment destroy the match of the entire prefix, which is the exact opposite of the feature. Digests, counts and every other changing diagnostic live in the sidecar; the section boundaries inside the text stay fixed (`#SYS-SEGMENT-FRAMING`). PROP-009 `#ARTIFACTS-CARRY-NO-TOKEN-BUDGET` already settles that a generated boot artifact carries no size budget, and the same reasoning applies here: the prefix's size is the sum of what the resolution says the session must have, and padding it to reach a provider's minimum cacheable length is explicitly forbidden (`#SYS-CACHE-ECONOMICS`).

p.SYS-DETERMINISM: **Determinism is a property with named mechanics.** The segment order is fixed by `#SYS-BAND-ORDER`; the framing, encoding (UTF-8, no BOM) and line endings are fixed by `#SYS-SEGMENT-FRAMING`; the continuation plan's order is the existing INDEX order and no other traversal; and nothing is summarised, re-wrapped, sorted by an unordered map, or stamped. The claim to be proved is therefore mechanical and testable: two checkouts of the same commit in different directories, on Linux, macOS and Windows, produce byte-identical `SYSTEM.md` and `SYSTEM.meta.json`, and a repeated generation with unchanged inputs rewrites neither file (`#SYS-NO-EQUAL-REWRITE`), so it does not even move an mtime.

p.SYS-INVALIDATION: **The invalidation table — what each kind of change does.** It is the user-facing summary of `#SYS-CONTINUATION-WITNESS-IS-RUNTIME` and the one thing a reader needs to predict the feature's behaviour.

identity.fence: change effect on the prefix / the request -------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------- new question, time, current plan, cwd nothing; only band T changes. The prefix is never built from any of these values. bytes of an applicable dynamic boot file, prefix unchanged and still valid; a fresh band U/G plan unchanged suffix is read per request. Existing installed- integrity rules continue to apply. template, entrypoint, static-lane input, prefix stale. `check` says so and names why; recipe or lane_form regeneration is explicit. Stale bytes are never sent as current. INDEX composition or order, a condition, the pairing is invalid: recompute the boot plan and visibility, selected node, package binding republish the affected artifacts. Never mix two generations of prefix and sidecar. model, tools, SDK wrapper, request framing the file may be identical while the provider's actual cached prefix differs. A local digest is not a remote cache identity. provider TTL expiry a new cache write may be needed with a completely unchanged SYSTEM.md.

p.SYS-BASELINE-CORRECTIONS: **Decided 2026-11-10 — where the 2026-11-07 research was wrong about the code, recorded so the plan's baseline is not re-derived.** Verified against `e2508fc1d`. **(1)** `own_boot.rs` is **not** `crates/vibe-workspace/src/own_boot.rs`; it is `crates/vibe-workspace/src/install/bootgen/own_boot.rs` (226 lines), a private submodule declared at `install/bootgen.rs:346-347`. **(2)** `conditions.rs` is **not** under `boot_artifacts/`; it is `crates/vibe-workspace/src/install/bootgen/conditions.rs` (97 lines), used from `install/bootgen.rs:60`. **(3)** `legacy_entries` does **not** exclude "only" the three generated names: it also skips non-regular files (`:177-179`) and everything `vibe_specdoc::is_spec_source` rejects (`:181-183`), and it hard-errors on a Markdown/XML name collision (`:212-222`) — which matters, because `is_spec_source` accepts by extension alone, so both new `.md` paths are admitted today and `#SYS-SELF-INCLUSION`'s gate is required, not optional. **(4)** `generated_boot_paths` is private and returns boot-dir-relative **paths**, not bare names (`layout.rs:250-255`), so the reservation is an edit to that one private list plus two new public accessors, not a new predicate per caller. **(5)** The research's own refusal to trust a source comment was right: the unresolved-link fallback in `boot.rs:355-359` is `unwrap_or_default()` and `LinkType`'s `#[default]` sits on `Dynamic` (`crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/package.rs:405`), while the comment at `boot.rs:352-354` says the final fallback is `static` and is wrong. **(6)** The boot transaction's role set is **closed and validated**, not open: `boot_artifacts/transaction/journal.rs:62-86` admits exactly `INDEX.md`, `STATIC.md` and `STATIC.xml` as production targets, requires the selected/stale pair to be exactly that distinct `STATIC` pair (`:75-78`), and `transaction.rs:259-282` requires all targets to share one parent directory and be distinct — so `#SYS-TRANSACTION-ROLES` is a real change to that owner and nothing about a new filename is transactionally covered by default. The durable record is not called `Transaction`: `journal.rs:7-10` aliases the wire type `BootArtifactTransaction` as `Journal`, and the write input is `ArtifactWrite` (`transaction.rs:61-67`), holding the INDEX bytes, the optional selected STATIC bytes and the stale spelling to remove. **(7)** There is **not** one semantic lane compiler call but **three** independent prepare-and-compile sites, as `#SYS-LANE-VERBATIM` now records; a change to lane preparation must move all three, and a design that assumed one seam would silently miss the owner-managed and custom-backend lanes. **(8)** Four more research paths are wrong, all under `crates/vibe-workspace/src/`: `publish_node_boot` is `install/bootgen/publication.rs:13`, not `boot_artifacts/publication.rs`; the unit fingerprint is `boot/hybrid/fingerprint.rs`, not `install/bootgen/fingerprint.rs`, which does not exist; owner-plan digest frames are `install/bootgen/owner_plans.rs:15`, not `boot_artifacts/owner_plans.rs`; static-zone membership and order are `boot/hybrid.rs` with hoisting in `boot/hybrid/hoist.rs`, not `boot_artifacts/hybrid.rs`; and the node-dependency projection is `install/bootgen/node_dependency.rs:14`. **(9)** The research's "StaticTransitive forces descendants **except residual OS gates**" is **wrong at HEAD**: `boot/hybrid.rs:244-288` `descend` never consults a contribution's `when`, and says so in code at `:263-265` — a gated target joins the static zone like any other, and gates act later, in `has_static_boot` / `static_boot_count` (`:135-151`) and in the fragment filter of `install/bootgen/node_dependency.rs:108-111`. Four doc comments still claim the old behaviour (`boot/hybrid.rs:17-20`, `:118-121`, `boot/hybrid/fingerprint.rs:10-11`, `boot/hybrid/hoist.rs:16`); they are stale and must not be cited as behaviour. This matters here only as a warning about the source of truth, since `#SYS-NO-FROZEN-INDEX` keeps every gate in band G regardless. **(10)** `vibe check` does **not** validate the spec-XML dialect, and no `cargo xtask` subcommand or test walks `vibevm/vibespecs/**` to parse it; the only authoritative validator is the PROP-045 projector `vibe_specdoc::project_spec_text` (`crates/vibe-specdoc/src/load.rs:140`), reached corpus-wide through `vibe facts check` or per file through `vibe refactor convert-source --dry-run`, which parses but always exits 0. Adding a dialect check is a candidate recorded in the app-versions campaign log, not a thing this campaign may assume exists.

p.SYS-CAPTURE-REUSE: **Decided 2026-11-10 — capture reuses the existing retained observations and adds no new reader.** The prefix's inputs are admitted through the owners that already hold them under a held workspace: the prepared node boot carrier with its observed policy, media and bytes (`install/bootgen/own_boot.rs`, whose `PreparedNodeBoot` holds `entries`, `root`, `relative`, `policy` and `captured`, and whose `recheck()` re-validates them), the declared-source bindings and generated observations (`boot_artifacts/declared_sources.rs`), the generated-input admission that captures before and after verification and refuses stale unit freshness (`install/bootgen/generated_inputs.rs`), and the read-only in-memory lane analysis (`install/bootgen/analyze.rs`). Three things capture does **not** do: it does not expand a home directory, a stewardship file, a plan, a custody record or a token path because some authored sentence mentions one (`#SYS-NO-HOME-EXPANSION`); it does not recursively follow prose links, `spec://` references or `#use` markers; and it does not read the whole host inventory — the scope is the selected node's boot scope, exactly as PROP-072 `#SOURCE-HOST-BOOT-LAW` bounds it. Classification is kept separate per lane: an INDEX row is classified as a continuation row, not as a static-link contribution, and the two are never merged into one list.

p.SYS-PROSPECTIVE-ENTRYPOINT: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the entrypoint witness is the prospective one of the same generation, never the file as it was before the write.** The same publication can rewrite the entrypoint's managed block: `boot_artifacts.rs:365` `write_boot_artifacts_inner` compiles the INDEX body and the static artifact first (`:379-391`), then calls `transaction::write_production_with_selectors` (`:405`) whose selector closure (`:413-415`) runs `redirect::write_redirect_blocks_with_transaction` **after** the INDEX/STATIC roll-forward commits (`transaction.rs:245`), and the replacement content itself depends on the target spec format. Witnessing the pre-write entrypoint would make a newly published prefix stale the instant it was written, or bind it to the wrong generation. So the prospective managed-redirect projection is computed through that same redirect owner, the source-before and expected-source-after are retained separately, and the prefix, the sidecar and any changed redirect are published and checked as **one coherent generation**. The entrypoint is never re-read after publication to manufacture agreeing evidence.

p.SYS-TRANSACTION-ROLES: **Decided 2026-11-10 — two new production roles inside the existing boot transaction, and no second atomicity story.** `SYSTEM.md` and `SYSTEM.meta.json` become two new `StageRole`s and two new admitted production targets in `boot_artifacts/transaction/journal.rs` (whose target list `:21-23` and validation `:62-86` are closed today), staged in `transaction/prepare.rs` and applied beside the INDEX and STATIC roll-forwards in `transaction.rs`. They are *inside* the existing commit, not a parallel writer: a failure must never leave a new prefix paired with a sidecar of another generation, nor damage the previous usable set. The whole output set is computed and validated **before** publication, the relevant captured inputs are rechecked immediately before the write (as `boot_artifacts.rs:402-404` already does), and the selected-source-member protection of PROP-009 `#ARTIFACTS-PAIR` is preserved unchanged: `crates/vibe-workspace/src/install/bootgen/publication.rs:13` `publish_node_boot` refuses to publish into a nonroot authored package member selected as a dependency by `(kind, group, name)` with version absent from the predicate (`:24-28`), and the two new roles are inside that same refusal rather than beside it. The `common_parent` invariant (`transaction.rs:259-282`) holds trivially, since all five targets live in the one boot directory. There is no second journal.

p.SYS-NO-EQUAL-REWRITE: **Equal bytes are not rewritten.** Publication already skips a write whose content equals what is on disk (`boot_artifacts/redirect.rs:267-269` and `transaction/selector.rs:21-23`), and the two new roles use the same rule, so an idempotent regeneration produces no write, no mtime change and no git diff — which is also the mechanical form of the first acceptance condition. A regeneration must never grow the file: the same inputs give the same length, and a prefix that grows on a second run is a self-inclusion bug by definition.

p.SYS-REMOVAL-AND-CONFLICT: **Decided 2026-11-10 — opting out, and the file that is not ours.** Removing `SYSTEM-TEMPLATE.md` makes the node opt out, and the next install removes exactly the two outputs it can prove it owns — proof being the sidecar's own witness of the pair, by the same reasoning the publication already uses to delete the *stale* STATIC spelling while never touching the selected one (`boot_artifacts.rs:401`, `transaction/prepare.rs:90`). A `SYSTEM.md` present with **no** sidecar, with a sidecar that does not describe it, or whose bytes do not match the sidecar's `prefix_sha256`, is an **ownership conflict**: a named refusal that writes nothing and deletes nothing, because a file by that name may be a user's own work. A hand-edited output is never silently blessed as current and never silently overwritten; the user is told which file, which mismatch, and the exact command that would regenerate it deliberately. Switching lane spelling, changing the entrypoint or changing the recipe is an ordinary regeneration of a coherent set, not a removal.

p.SYS-OPERATIONS-SURFACE: **Decided 2026-11-10 — generation on install, and one new top-level command namespace with three verbs.** Generation happens inside the install, reinstall, format-change and staged-publication paths that already publish boot artifacts, for every node that has opted in; nothing is generated at session boot, and boot stays pure file reading. The explicit surface is `vibe prompt`, a free top-level name today: **`vibe prompt build`** writes the outputs through `#SYS-TRANSACTION-ROLES`; **`vibe prompt check [--json]`** compares the current inputs with the published artifacts and reports `equal` / `stale` / `missing` / `conflict` / `unavailable` / `freshness_unverifiable` with the reasons; **`vibe prompt prepare --json`** returns the materials of `#SYS-CONTINUATION-CACHEABLE` — bands P, U and G separately, with their observed digests, the recommended cache boundaries and the unresolved remainder. `prepare` returns **materials and observations, never a ready-to-send request**: it does not assemble credentials, choose a model or construct a provider envelope, and its grammar is settled together with its first real consumer rather than shipped as flags that parse and are ignored.

p.SYS-READ-ONLY-CHECK: **Decided 2026-11-10 — `check` and `prepare` are effect-free, and the boundary is a capability contract rather than a sandbox promise.** Neither writes a product, cache, profile or config file; neither opens a network connection; and — the part that is easy to get wrong — neither invokes an effectful native or backend compile provider to recompute freshness. Reusing an analyse entrypoint is not by itself proof of that, and the distinction is per function rather than per module: `analyze_node_lane` (`install/bootgen/analyze.rs:80`) takes no provider and is effect-free, while `analyze_node_lane_bound_native_using` (`:270`), `analyze_effective_bound_native_with_sources` (`:554`) and `compile_node_backend_using` (`:415`) each accept an `OwnerNativeCompileProvider` — the last one mandatorily — and hand control to a caller-supplied trait whose invocation may spawn a process or reach the network (`boot_artifacts/native_managed/explicit.rs:71-73`, `native_managed.rs:332`), with native continuations bound to owner runtime epochs. So "we called analyse" establishes nothing; naming the exact function does. What `check`/`prepare` may do is read retained inputs, compare witnesses, and run only explicitly effect-free builtin preparation. When the needed proof is impossible without an effectful provider — a pending native unit, a stale generated substitution, an unadmittable generated input — the answer is `freshness_unverifiable` or `unavailable` **with** the explicit `vibe prompt build` that would resolve it. It never falls back to an empty transform plan, never quietly repairs while promising no writes, and never becomes an implicit install. `prepare` is the calling program's preflight, run outside the model's turn; the transport contract never asks an agent to run it (`#SYS-TRANSPORT-CONTRACT`).

p.SYS-SESSION-TARGET: **Decided 2026-11-10 — a gated row is evaluated against an explicitly supplied session target, never against the generator's host.** The condition grammar is closed and already exact: `crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/package/when.rs:71-112` accepts `os:windows` / `os:macos` / `os:linux` and `installed:<group>/<name>` and refuses anything else by name, and the enum has exactly those two variants. `installed:` is a **generation-time** decision owned by `install/bootgen/conditions.rs:86-96` — false drops the contribution entirely, true removes the condition — so only an `os:` gate survives into band G. `prepare` therefore requires an explicit session target when band G is non-empty; an absent or unknown target is **unresolved input**, reported as such, and never resolved to the operating system of whatever machine once generated the prefix. An unknown selector never becomes `true`. The prefix itself stays portable: baking an OS into it is the alternative in `#SYS-OWNER-QUESTIONS` Q3, and it is not the default.

api.title: 8. The API boundary, authority and agent modes

p.SYS-ROLE-PLACEMENT: **Decided 2026-11-10 — a filename chooses no API role, and moving repository text into an instruction role is not semantically neutral.** A supported adapter places the project's trusted instructions explicitly in a supported instruction role (`system`, `developer`, or the equivalent provider field), preserving any mandatory external instructions and the user-set boundaries that already apply. The elevation is acknowledged rather than assumed away: project instructions, package boot text, examples and operational grants do not acquire provider-level authority merely by being on disk or by being in a file called `SYSTEM.md`, and a text separator inside one message creates no real role boundary. The one thing a repository file cannot do is fix an agent that does not let its caller control its own prefix or its auto-loading; such an agent is simply not part of the guaranteed integration, and saying so is more useful than pretending a Markdown file solves it.

p.SYS-NO-DOUBLE-INJECTION: **A supported adapter never injects the prefix and then auto-loads the same entrypoint or lane again.** Supplied sources are accounted for explicitly, which is the only reason the transport contract can say what it says. Double injection is the failure this feature most plausibly produces — it would double the cost it exists to reduce while leaving the agent two copies of the same instructions — so it is a named qualification scenario proved by capturing the actual request against a local fake provider, not an assurance.

p.SYS-WORKER-EXCLUSION: **Decided 2026-11-10 — a quiet worker does not receive the central prefix at all, not even briefly.** The profile and the packet are selected **before** the request is constructed, so the central prefix is never assembled for a bounded worker; there is no "ignore the parts that do not apply to you" clause in the prefix and there is deliberately no attempt to write one. A later message cannot return spent context and cannot restore a delegation boundary that has already been crossed. A central session gets the profile of its own selected node; a root's legitimate aggregation of its own subtree stays legitimate (PROP-009 `#MATRYOSHKA-SCOPES`), and the rule is "no content from outside the selected effective scope", not "no members".

p.SYS-NO-HOME-EXPANSION: **Nothing user-local is pulled in by reference.** An authored instruction that *mentions* a home directory, a stewardship settings or plan file, a custody or handoff record, or a token path is an instruction to a tool-using agent, not permission to embed that file's contents; the exporter opens none of them. Package boot text and ordinary repository documents do not acquire instruction authority just because they sit on disk and are reachable. Legitimate user-local observations reach a session through an explicit runtime contract in band T, chosen per request by the caller — which is also what keeps an ostensibly shared prefix from differing by user and from accidentally publishing confidential material. The qualification for this is a sentinel test: the files exist, and they are proved never opened and never present in the output.

p.SYS-CACHE-FACTS: **Checked provider properties, 2026-11-07, recorded as evidence and not as a product contract.** OpenAI: the cache depends on matching the actual rendered prefix, including tools and other request parts; a stable instruction block helps, while retention, eligibility and write conditions depend on the model, and the hit must be read from real usage. Anthropic: the Messages API takes `cache_control` and the hierarchy is tools, then system, then messages, so a change to an early block affects later matches, and entries have a limited lifetime. Gemini: implicit caching exists and a common early prefix is recommended, while explicit caching depends on the API and model and is not universal. Specific prices, TTLs and model lists are deliberately **not** frozen into this document: they change, and a design that encoded them would be wrong within a quarter. A text artifact is not a portable KV cache, does not transfer between models or providers, does not by itself reduce the amount of context a session needs, and does not reconcile contradictory instructions. Stabilising a large prefix is not the same as deserving one: whether the boot a session loads should be that large at all remains a separate engineering question this feature does not answer.

p.SYS-CACHE-ECONOMICS: **The economics are parametric, and a saving is claimed only when measured.** For a prefix of L tokens with W cache writes and H cache reads, compare `L × (W + H) × uncached_rate` against `L × (W × write_rate + H × read_rate) + storage_cost` where storage is billed, then add the uncacheable requests and the unchanged cost of the dynamic and output tokens. The numbers come from the current rates and the observed usage, never from this document. A first request and frequent expiries can reduce or erase the benefit entirely. Byte repeatability and the exact request envelope are provable offline against a fake provider; a claim about real money requires a separate measurement of cache write and read tokens, latency and cost on named models, which is **not** performed by this design and is authorised separately (`#SYS-OWNER-QUESTIONS` Q5). Padding a prefix with useless text to reach a provider's minimum cacheable length is forbidden outright.

layering.title: 9. Forward compatibility with the user and override layers

p.SYS-LAYER-ROLE: **Decided 2026-11-10 — this document specifies the `project` layer of PROP-074 `#LAYERED-PREFIX`, and says so in the artifact.** That fact composes one cache-stable prefix from the project layer, the global user project and the project override, in the precedence order of PROP-074 `#OVERRIDE-PRECEDENCE`, with the project layer **first** precisely because it is the most shared and most stable, so that the project's own prefix stays a byte-identical leading part of the composed one. The sidecar therefore carries `layer = "project"` from version 1 and every segment id is layer-qualified from version 1, even though no other layer exists yet. Without a user project or override the composed prefix **is** the project prefix, so the artifact this document specifies is already the whole answer for a project that composes nothing.

p.SYS-LAYER-CONCATENATION: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the four properties that let a later campaign compose layers with no format change here.** **(1) No document-level frame.** The prefix has no opening or closing wrapper, no table of contents and no "this document has N parts" preamble; every separator between *layers* belongs to the composer, and the project layer's bytes end with exactly one LF so a following layer concatenates cleanly (`#SYS-SEGMENT-FRAMING`). **(2) No total digest in the text.** `prefix_sha256` is the project layer's own digest and lives in the sidecar; the composite's digest is the composer's own artifact and never appears inside any layer, so adding a layer cannot change a byte of the project layer. **(3) Layer-qualified ids.** Segment ids and input roles are namespaced by layer, so two layers' sidecars merge without collision and a composer can address one segment of one layer. **(4) A layer-scoped transport contract.** The contract of `#SYS-TRANSPORT-CONTRACT` speaks only for its own layer's supplied sources, so a composer appends each layer's contract instead of regenerating one global one. The composed prefix is personal and must never be committed, which is PROP-074 `#LAYERED-PREFIX-LOCATION`'s rule and that campaign's business — this document's artifacts are committed, and the two are different files in different places.

p.SYS-LAYER-NO-FORMAT-CHANGE: **The prediction this section makes, so it can be falsified.** When the layered-prefix campaign lands, it adds a composer and a personal uncommitted output; it must need **no** change to `vibe-system-prompt/1`, to the segment framing, to the transport-contract recipe or to the three reserved paths. If it does need one, this section was wrong, and the honest record of that is an amendment to this fact rather than a quiet format bump.

formats.title: 10. Format and wire changes

p.SYS-FORMAT-CHANGES: **Decided 2026-11-10 — every format and wire surface this task touches.** The regime at writing is `formats/EPOCHS.toml` `public = false`, `break_window_open = true`: breaking is free and unmigrated, no break note under `formats/breaks/` is required, and the standing user recipe is "regenerate / re-init / re-fetch" (PROP-044 `##THE-PUBLIC-SWITCH`). A format must exist in `formats/REGISTRY.toml` or `FormatId` cannot express it. Each entry also carries its change-log line in `campaigns/sys-prompt-2026-11/FORMAT-CHANGES.md` with ids `SP-FMT-NNN`.

[format.boot-system-prompt] (generated UTF-8 text, no schema) segment framing, LF, no BOM, nothing volatile generated sidecar (new) schemas/system_prompt_meta.jtd.json new, 1 vibe-system-prompt/1: inputs, [format.boot-system-meta] segments, continuation plan, layer role; no timestamp, no absolute path, no continuation content digest package manifest (schema = "none", authored TOML) 1 -> 1 [system_prompt] with [format.manifest] entrypoint, lane_form, recipe; all optional and omitted when absent, so existing manifests are byte-identical boot publication transaction (internal journal, .vibe-boot-*) n/a two new StageRoles and two new (no registered format) admitted production targets in transaction/journal.rs; the closed role validation and the common-parent invariant learn them prompt check (new) schemas/prompt_check.jtd.json new, 1 vibe-prompt-check/1: the verdict [format.cli-prompt-check] and the reason list prompt prepare (new) schemas/prompt_prepare.jtd.json new, 1 vibe-prompt-prepare/1: bands P, [format.cli-prompt-prepare] U, G as separate materials with observed digests, recommended cache boundaries, unresolved remainder vibe check (existing check inventory) 1 -> 1 one new check id for a stale or [format.cli-check-report] conflicting SYSTEM artifact adapter request capture (new) schemas/prompt_request_capture.jtd.json new, 1 the fake-provider envelope the [format.cli-prompt-capture] qualification scenarios assert: roles, block order, tool position, prefix boundary, and the provider usage counters read back from a real response

p.SYS-OWNER-QUESTIONS: **Open to the owner, each with the default this design takes unless the owner says otherwise.** **(Q1) Is the unconditional INDEX band a cacheable continuation, or baked into the prefix?** Default: **cacheable continuation** (`#SYS-CONTINUATION-CACHEABLE`) — the bytes are cached either way, and baking them would contradict `kind = "static"`'s actual meaning, make freshness much harder to prove, and buy nothing. The alternative, a target-bound fully-frozen snapshot, is a genuinely different contract with a freshness limit, and it would have to be offered as a second profile rather than as this one's default. **(Q2) What override authority do repository, package and user-preference instructions have once they sit in the API instruction role?** Default: the project layer is a trusted application scaffold carrying scoped project policy, user-local preference material never enters the prefix at all, and mandatory external instructions and user-set boundaries are preserved above it; the design does **not** assume the agent-side override semantics carry over unchanged, because the role is not the same role. **(Q3) Portable prefix with gated continuation, or target-bound prefix?** Default: **portable** — OS gates stay in band G and are evaluated against an explicitly supplied session target (`#SYS-SESSION-TARGET`), which is what the committed INDEX design already does; a target-bound prefix is cheaper to send and strictly less reusable, and nothing in this repository needs it today, since every INDEX row here is currently unconditional. **(Q4) How much of the entrypoint must be represented byte-for-byte, versus authored afresh in the template?** Default: **all of it, verbatim**, with the one in-place managed-block substitution of `#SYS-REDIRECT-IN-PLACE` — because no generic prose filter can infer which paragraphs the owner wants dropped, and silently dropping instructions is the worst available failure. The honest cost is `#SYS-ENTRYPOINT-IS-AN-INPUT`: a frequently-edited entrypoint means a frequently-rebuilt prefix, and the remedy is repository hygiene, not an exporter heuristic. **(Q5) Must a measured provider saving exist before the campaign closes?** Default: **no** — the campaign ships the parametric model, the method and the offline envelope proof, and a live cache measurement on named models is a separately authorised follow-up that spends real money and is never run inside the campaign (`#SYS-CACHE-ECONOMICS`). **(Q6) Are the two generated artifacts committed, like `STATIC`/`INDEX`?** Default: **yes, git-tracked and marked generated** (PROP-009 `#ARTIFACTS-GENERATED`), so a fresh clone needs no build; the alternative — generated and ignored — would make the prefix unavailable to exactly the zero-dependency case the boot model exists for.

p.SYS-ACCEPTANCE: **The twelve conditions the feature is accepted against**, carried forward from the owner's research proposal and made mechanical where it was prose. (1) The same inputs give a byte-identical `SYSTEM.md` and `SYSTEM.meta.json` in different checkout locations and on Linux, macOS and Windows; a repeated generation neither grows the file nor rewrites it. (2) Neither the template nor either output becomes an ordinary boot input, in legacy discovery or in declared mode; a direct or indirect self-include is refused before any write; a prose mention is not a self-include. (3) Differential scenarios confirm the prefix's static-first order, the continuation's original INDEX order, installed visibility, and gate behaviour for all three operating systems. (4) XML, Markdown, mixed and generated-stream lanes are handled by their existing owners; an authored literal directive or fenced example never becomes an executable import. (5) Root, member and specspace profiles receive nothing outside their selected effective scope while a root's permitted subtree aggregation is preserved, and a quiet worker never receives the central prefix, even temporarily. (6) A change of dynamic bytes under a compatible plan changes only the fresh suffix; a change of the template, the entrypoint or the lane makes the prefix detectably stale with no hidden rebuild. (7) A missing, unsupported or mutated input, an invalid marker and an output conflict each leave the previous coherent set intact. (8) Home, plan, custody and token sentinel files are never opened and never appear in the output without an explicit separate runtime input; the current task and time never change the prefix. (9) A fake provider sees the exact roles, block and tool order, prefix boundary and the absence of a duplicate entrypoint injection — and this does not count as a live cache hit. (10) `check` and `prepare` are proved read-only by filesystem, network and provider-call sentinels; no effectful callback runs even on a cache miss; install, reinstall and publish go through the one transaction owner. (11) The sidecar format and the invalidation reasons are versioned; an old consumer need not read the new artifact, and a project without the opt-in boots exactly as before. (12) A saving is claimed only after a separate provider measurement, and no useless text is ever added to reach a cache threshold.

p.changelog: 2026-11-10: adopted as a framework record from the owner's research proposal of 2026-11-07 and settled against the tree at `e2508fc1d` as campaign node `SYS-PROMPT`, after `APP-VERSIONS`. The design resolves the proposal's open choices in `#SYS-BANDS`, `#SYS-BAND-ORDER`, `#SYS-NO-FROZEN-INDEX`, `#SYS-CONTINUATION-CACHEABLE`, `#SYS-MANIFEST-TABLE`, `#SYS-LAYOUT-RESERVATION`, `#SYS-SELF-INCLUSION`, `#SYS-REDIRECT-IN-PLACE`, `#SYS-TRANSPORT-CONTRACT`, `#SYS-LANE-VERBATIM`, `#SYS-LANE-SPELLING`, `#SYS-SEGMENT-FRAMING`, `#SYS-SIDECAR`, `#SYS-CONTINUATION-WITNESS-IS-RUNTIME`, `#SYS-PROSPECTIVE-ENTRYPOINT`, `#SYS-TRANSACTION-ROLES`, `#SYS-REMOVAL-AND-CONFLICT`, `#SYS-OPERATIONS-SURFACE`, `#SYS-READ-ONLY-CHECK` and `#SYS-SESSION-TARGET`; `#SYS-LAYER-ROLE`, `#SYS-LAYER-CONCATENATION` and `#SYS-LAYER-NO-FORMAT-CHANGE` bind the artifact to PROP-074 `#LAYERED-PREFIX` so the later composition campaign needs no format change here; section 10 is the format inventory `#SYS-FORMAT-CHANGES`; and `#SYS-BASELINE-CORRECTIONS` records the ten places the 2026-11-07 survey was wrong about the code, seven of them wrong file paths and three wrong behavioural claims — including its assumption of a single lane compiler seam, where there are three. Six questions remain genuinely the owner's, each with its default, in `#SYS-OWNER-QUESTIONS`. Nothing is implemented; every fact is `spec/plan`.
